producer_report.summary: I added a class-of-work trend measure and gave OLY-9-10 a mechanism. The new module `class_trend.rs` takes landed jobs by landing order and groups them by class of work. A class with at least 4 landed jobs gets the median total minutes of its older half compared with its newer half. A fall is reported as improving. A rise is reported as worse, naming the landed job that came just before the class's minutes rose above every older job and stayed there. `athena status` prints this as a `trend` line, and the line is absent when no class has enough jobs. `docs/spec.toml` now names the module as the mechanism, keeps owner Hestia, and the measure ends `status: trend`. I also added the label to the status label list, a `class_trend` field on the status view, and a CHANGELOG entry.

checks_run.note: fmt --check had flagged one assert in class_trend.rs; formatted. Not rerun as a check afterwards.

criteria_check.criterion: docs/spec.toml requirement OLY-9-10 has mechanism naming crates/athena-core/src/class_trend.rs (a file that exists), keeps owner Hestia, and a measure ending with `status: trend`; STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs contains the `trend` label.
criteria_check.evidence: Edited docs/spec.toml (mechanism names class_trend.rs, owner Hestia, measure ends `status: trend`); added ("trend", "class_trend") to STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS; cargo test -p xtask spec tests pass.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core class_trend`: a test builds landed jobs of one class whose minutes fall from older to newer and asserts the class is reported improving; another builds a class whose minutes rise after a named earlier job and asserts that job id is reported as making it worse; a class with too few jobs is not reported. These tests fail if compute returns nothing.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran it: 4 pass (improving, worse naming job x, too few jobs gives None, unchanged class). The improving and worse tests call expect() on analyze, so they fail if it returns nothing.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core every_measure_label_names_a_status_view_field_and_a_printed_line`: passes with the new `trend` label, proving StatusView has class_trend and `athena status` prints a line starting `trend `.
criteria_check.evidence: Ran it: passes. StatusView has `pub class_trend:`; display.rs contains "trend       {line}".

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`: a status rendering test shows the `trend` line text with improving and worse classes; and the xtask/spec test over docs/spec.toml passes (`cargo test --workspace`).
criteria_check.evidence: Ran `cargo test -p athena-cli the_trend_line` (display::tests::the_trend_line_lists_improving_and_worse_classes passes) and `cargo test -p xtask` (spec and policy tests pass). The full athena-cli and workspace suites were not run.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass.
The trend section is absent (no line) when no class has enough landed jobs, so an empty history is not shown as success.
criteria_check.evidence: analyze returns None when no class has 4 jobs (test a_class_with_too_few_jobs_is_not_reported, including the empty input); display.rs prints the trend section only when class_trend is Some, and the field is skipped in serialization when None.

open_issues: Not run: the policy scan after the final edits, clippy, the full workspace tests, and a status-level end-to-end test over real job records. I ran `cargo test -p xtask` earlier, which includes the policy scan, and it passed before the final fmt run.
`trend` is not in hestia.rs SPEED_LABELS, so OLY-9-10 requests keep normal priority. Adding it would make them urgent.
mistakes: The first draft named the rise using the older-half median as the threshold. That named the wrong job in my own test. I changed the threshold to the highest minutes in the older half.
learnings: JobState lives in crate::store, not crate::state.
landed_jobs() carries no class; the class comes from JobRecords::class(), joined by job id.
The label test only searches status.rs, display.rs and hestia.rs for a string starting with the quoted label and a space.
